transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

Many ovens won't heat at all after a power cut (or with an end time set) until the clock is set or manual mode is selected — often a hand symbol, or holding two buttons together; the manual shows how. Was the clock flashing or set to an auto / timer mode, or was it already showing the time in manual mode?
clock shows the time n nothing flashing, its in manual i think. still no heat

Thanks for confirming that. Please check the control knobs quickly. Since the fan runs during defrost without heat, ensure the function knob is set to a fan-oven symbol (a fan inside a ring) and not defrost, light-only or eco mode. Also make sure the temperature dial is turned up until the temperature indicator light switches on. Was it on one of those other settings, or was it already on a heating function with the temperature up?
its on the fan oven symbol, temp turned up and the little orange light comes on n stays on. just no heat

To match the right part for your oven I need its exact model. Could you send me the model number? It's usually on a label around the oven door opening or on the back / underside of the door — a photo is fine.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its on the rating plate on the door frame, says IFW 6330 IX. its an Indesit built in single oven, bout 7 yrs old

[Heading: Fan-oven element]
Thank you for providing the model details. The symptoms you described point to the fan-oven element. I have located the correct replacement part for your Indesit IFW6330IX below. If you choose to fit it yourself, please ensure the oven is switched off at the isolator and allowed to cool completely before starting, as the element is located behind the back panel inside the unit. Alternatively, you may prefer to have a qualified appliance engineer carry out this repair for you.
